methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
OSH Cut is a bootstrapped robotics and manufacturing company founded by Caleb and Jacom Chamberlain with no disclosed prior funding. The valuation universe comprises 10 peers in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms such as Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this analysis. Despite identifying 10 same-sector comparables, none met the narrow stage and tier filters required for robust triangulation. The company's bootstrapped status and absence of disclosed valuation history meant zero matches at the same development stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero within comparable valuation tiers. Applying a sector-wide median would introduce substantial distortion given the heterogeneity of company sizes, technologies, and revenue profiles across robotics manufacturing.

Without a sufficiently tight peer cohort and absent revenue, profitability, or other financial metrics in the data provided, a triangulated valuation cannot be responsibly derived. Any estimate would rest on either: (1) extrapolation from the public comparable (277810.KQ), which lacks specificity to OSH Cut's stage and business model, or (2) sector-wide private medians, which would conflate early-stage bootstrapped ventures with well-funded growth-stage robotics firms. Further diligence—including detailed financial performance, customer traction, and technical differentiation—is necessary before a defensible valuation range can be established.
